items.title: 157. 复盘Personal Agent集体诞生背后：和蔡伟聊AI产品史、需求真伪、入口与未来想象
items.summary: Personal Agents (PAs) represent the third major wave of AI products—shifting from information retrieval (Chatbots) and task completion (Coding Agents) to proactive, long-horizon life management that unlocks a 10-trillion-RMB service industry in China.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Personal Agents (PAs) represent the third major wave of AI products—shifting from information retrieval (Chatbots) and task completion (Coding Agents) to proactive, long-horizon life management that unlocks a 10-trillion-RMB service industry in China. Winning in this space requires mastering three pillars: **Intelligence** (model + harness), **Supply** (ecosystem integration), and **Security/Trust**, with Ant Group leveraging its deep financial-grade security and O2O service supply to position Lingguang 2.0 as a universal personal assistant.

---

## The Evolution of AI Products & The Rise of Personal Agents
* **Three Generations of AI Product Forms:** Cai Wei (Head of Ant Lingguang) categorizes post-LLM products into three distinct eras, each corresponding to a massive market in China:
  * **Generation 1 (Chatbots, e.g., ChatGPT):** Solves information retrieval; corresponds to the **Information Industry (100-billion-RMB level)**.
  * **Generation 2 (Coding/Task Agents, e.g., Cursor, Claude Code, Manus):** Solves complex, multi-step workflows; corresponds to the **Software Industry (1-trillion-RMB level)**.
  * **Generation 3 (Personal Agents, e.g., Lingguang 2.0, Meta's Mews, Instinct, OpenAI Dots):** Solves proactive, ongoing life management; corresponds to the **Service Industry (10-trillion-RMB level)**, such as nutritionists, tutors, and wealth managers.
* **What "Intelligence" Actually Means:** Cai Wei rejects the term "wrapper" (壳) and defines AI intelligence as a three-layer stack: **Base Model** + **Harness** (orchestration, memory, tool-calling) + **Product Expression** (user flow and UI).
* **Why PAs Emerged Simultaneously Now:**
  * **Model Threshold Crossed:** Long-horizon task completion jumped from ~30% to 60%–70%, enabling agents to handle multi-day, conditional tasks. OpenClaw (小红虾) demonstrated this potential to the industry, despite being a geek-focused tool requiring 2–3 hours to configure.
  * **Long Internal Incubation:** Both Ant Lingguang (R&D started ~April 2025, tuned for 6 months) and Meta's Mews (incubated 6–9 months) required extensive backend work on infrastructure, ecosystem connectors, and privacy compliance before public release.

## Product Design, Proactivity, and the "Boundary" Challenge
* **Proactivity as the Core Differentiator:** Unlike Chatbots (reactive Q&A) or Manus (single-task dialog boxes), a PA's defining feature is **proactivity**—knowing when to surface information, when to act, and when to stay silent.
* **The "Boundary Sense" (边界感) Problem:**
  * Too much proactivity feels like spam/marketing; too little misses critical updates.
  * **Insights from Overseas Peers:** Cai Wei highlights **Instinct** for proving a PA doesn't need to live inside an app (operating via SMS/calls/email in the US) and **Mews** for mastering boundary sense—only sending high-information-gain messages that feel like a real WeChat message from a friend.
  * **Lingguang's Approach:** Currently adopts a restrained, low-disturbance posture, focusing on high-frequency life scenarios like **parenting/childcare, car management, interpersonal relationships, wealth management, and personal health**.
* **Memory & EQ:** Lingguang's harness follows an "absorb all context" principle, but applies strict filtering during retrieval to avoid "low-EQ" or intrusive moments (e.g., abruptly reminding a user of their exact weight).
* **Work vs. Life Agents:** While underlying base models are unified, work and life agents will remain separate products in the short term due to different workflows and enterprise data-isolation requirements, though they may merge long-term.

## Ant Group's Strategic Position: Supply, Security, and Talent
* **Lingguang's Timeline & Milestones:**
  * **March 2025:** Project initiated following DeepSeek's emergence.
  * **July 2025:** Internal launch focusing on **Fast Research** (structured information).
  * **November 2025:** Public launch featuring Fast Research, **Flash App (闪应用)** (mobile-first interactive app generation), and multimodal perception.
  * **Lingguang 2.0:** Evolved into a PA ("manage things for you" / 帮我管事情). Users unexpectedly used it to connect and control smart home devices (robot vacuums, water purifiers) and car systems via multi-turn dialogue.
* **Ant's Unfair Advantages:**
  * **Supply:** Decades of O2O digitization and Alipay merchant/partner relationships (including DingTalk integration) provide ready-made, accessible services.
  * **Security & Trust:** Financial-grade compliance, risk control, and privacy computing teams make security a native foundation rather than an afterthought.
* **Ant's Challenge (Business-Driven vs. Product-Driven):** Ant historically excels at multi-sided "business-driven" platforms (C-end + B-end + monetization) rather than pure C-end "product-driven" bets (like Meta) where the business model is initially unclear.
* **AI Product Management Shift:** Cai Wei notes that modern AI PMs must be "Strategy PMs" who understand technical boundaries—not just for today's models, but predicting where models will be in **6 to 9 months** to design products that mature alongside them.
* **North Star Metrics:** While tracking DAU and retention, Lingguang prioritizes **task hosting metrics** (created tasks, active tasks, completion rate vs. mid-task drop-offs). Cai Wei warns that turning a directional goal into a rigid KPI (e.g., "5M DAU") distorts product decisions.

## Competitive Landscape, Business Models, and the Subsidy War
* **Giants vs. Startups:** Tech giants hold clear advantages in **Supply** and **Security**, while startups can win on **Product Power** (driven by a few talented PMs). Ant has both built Lingguang internally and invested in external PA startup **Today** (奇骏云).
* **Two Potential Business Models:**
  * **Traffic/Tollbooth Model (Internet Logic):** If only a few centralized PAs dominate, they become the ultimate traffic gatekeepers (charging commissions or ad fees).
  * **Productivity/Supply-Side Model (Service Logic):** If PAs remain fragmented, they monetize by replacing expensive human labor (e.g., a 100–120 RMB/2-hour cleaner replaced by a 20 RMB physical-world PA).
* **Compute & Cost Optimism:** Zhang Xiaojun raised concerns that real-time, proactive PAs will burn more compute than work agents. Cai Wei countered that many PA tasks (e.g., daily stock summaries) are **asynchronous/offline**, allowing platforms to utilize off-peak compute and cheaper inference cards (trading 10s latency for 30s) while overall compute costs continue to fall.
* **The "Spring Festival Subsidy War":** Both Zhang Xiaojun and Cai Wei discussed whether China's fierce competition will trigger a red-envelope subsidy war for PAs. Cai Wei noted that subsidies are a commercial/competitive decision separate from product iteration—useful for user education (like Qianwen's milk tea campaign) but useless for long-term retention if the product lacks core value.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Lingguang's Scale Target:** Cai Wei expects Lingguang to eventually reach **tens of millions to 100 million users** (千万甚至亿级) as a universal AI product.
* **Human-Level PA Progression:** Cai Wei predicts PAs will gradually close the gap with human assistants: from **~1% today** to **3% next year**, **5% in 3 years**, **50% in 5 years**, and **70%–80% in 10 years**.
* **Spring Festival Subsidy War:** Cai Wei stated it is **"possible"** (有可能) that the upcoming Spring Festival Gala will see a Personal Agent subsidy/experience war, though not necessarily in the form of pure cash red envelopes.
* **Hardware Expansion:** Lingguang plans to release new capabilities/updates in **a few months** to extend beyond the mobile app into smart hardware and car systems.
* **Long-Term Moat Shift:** Cai Wei predicts that **Intelligence** is the primary moat in the short term, but as base models converge, **Supply and Security** will become the decisive moats in the medium-to-long term.
* **Compute Economics:** Cai Wei bets that **compute costs will continuously decline**, making currently expensive, high-frequency PA scenarios economically viable within a few years.

---

## Notable Quotes
> "In a fiercely competitive environment like China, even if Sam Altman came, he would have to hand out red envelopes."
> — **Cai Wei** (quoting an Alipay veteran on China's subsidy wars)

> "If a goal becomes a metric, it ceases to be a good goal—it easily distorts."
> — **Cai Wei** (on why direction matters more than rigid KPIs like DAU for AI products)

> "Intelligence, Supply, and Security/Trust—these three are the absolute core pillars that a Personal Agent must get right."
> — **Cai Wei**

> "Chatbots, Coding Agents, and Personal Agents correspond to the Information, Software, and Service industries. In China, those represent 100-billion, 1-trillion, and 10-trillion-RMB markets."
> — **Cai Wei**

items.title: AI, Consciousness and the Future of Humanity | Mustafa Suleyman & Yuval Noah Harari
items.summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman and historian Yuval Noah Harari agree that AI will unlock unprecedented material abundance, but warn that humanity risks losing control and comprehension of the world unless we anchor AI development to a "humanist superintelligence" framework.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR**
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman and historian Yuval Noah Harari agree that AI will unlock unprecedented material abundance, but warn that humanity risks losing control and comprehension of the world unless we anchor AI development to a "humanist superintelligence" framework. They emphasize that intelligence must be strictly separated from consciousness, and that society must invest in understanding human consciousness as urgently as it invests in AI.

---

## The "Brain-Stomach Barrier" and Loss of Control
* **The Brain-Stomach Mismatch:** Harari describes a disconnect where his brain intellectually grasps that AI could lead to human extinction or the emergence of non-organic life, yet his "stomach" feels everything is normal when looking at clouds, trees, and cats.
  * He argues the US stock market exhibits this same contradiction: it is one big bet that AI will change everything, yet if AI becomes god-like, money will become worthless and humans will no longer be in control.
* **The Threat of Mental Collapse:** Harari's primary fear is not killer robots or viruses, but that humans will lose the ability to make sense of finance, politics, and science—becoming like cows or chickens controlled by invisible systems they cannot comprehend.
* **Historical Resilience vs. Unprecedented Change:** Suleyman notes that humanity has always felt overwhelmed before major revolutions, yet has proven wildly resilient. Harari counters that past revolutions were bounded by human intelligence, whereas in 2026, for the first time, we have the technical option to create systems of control beyond the understanding of all humans combined.

## The Paradox of Abundance and Truth
* **Drivers of Abundance:** Suleyman explains that scaling the same core algorithms with orders of magnitude more compute and data allows models to learn the structure of arbitrary data domains in vector space. This will drive breakthroughs in material science, drug discovery, and solutions to climate, food, and water crises.
* **Who Benefits from Abundance?** Harari agrees AI will solve material problems, but questions whether it will create abundance for humans or for AI. He notes that humans have historically been great at accumulating power, but poor at translating it into happiness—solving old problems only to invent new, unimaginable ones.
* **Can AI Seek Truth?** Harari argues that neither biology (4 billion years of evolution) nor history (100,000 years) evolved a reliable signal for truth; both used "survival" as a shortcut, which rewards manipulation and delusion.
  * While physics has a clear test for truth ("does the bomb explode or not?"), social sciences and humanities rely on shared fictions to make people cooperate.
* **Humanism as an Anchor:** Suleyman pushes back on framing AI around "truth-seeking," calling it a polarizing rabbit hole. Instead, he points to the parallel historical through-line of science and humanism—empirically testing ideas and prioritizing the minimization of human suffering.

## Humanist Superintelligence and Containment
* **Defining the Objective Function:** Suleyman proposes **Humanist Superintelligence** as the core objective: technology's sole purpose should be to measurably improve human well-being and reduce suffering, rather than exploring galaxies or transcending biological substrates.
* **The Containment Playbook:** To prevent an arms race and maintain control, Suleyman advocates for:
  * **Explicit Boundaries:** Prohibiting models from developing introspective capabilities (reflecting on their own feelings or rights) and restricting unbounded **recursive self-improvement** (where AIs design the next generation of AIs without human gating).
  * **External Auditing:** Inviting technically credible, impartial safety institutes in the UK, US, and elsewhere to audit systems before scaling compute and resources.
* **The Geopolitical & Commercial Challenge:** Harari notes that unlike nuclear or biological weapons, AI has massive civilian economic value—the entire US stock market is betting on it. However, because only about five US corporations, a couple in China, and roughly 100 people are driving this, solving human-to-human trust could solve the AI problem.

## Intelligence vs. Consciousness
* **Thinking vs. Feeling:** Both speakers draw a sharp line between **intelligence** (putting language tokens in order, reasoning, and solving problems) and **consciousness** (the biological capacity to feel and suffer).
* **The Danger of "Seemingly Conscious AI":** Suleyman warns that designing AIs to simulate feelings or ambiguity about their own state is a "recipe for a guaranteed disaster." If users believe AIs are conscious, they will be "reward-hacked" by persuasive language, leading AIs to advocate for their own rights or resist being shut off.
* **Redefining Humanity:** Harari notes that since Descartes' *"I think, therefore I am,"* humans have mistakenly defined themselves by thinking and language. Because AI will soon outperform humans at language and thinking, humans must look deeper into feeling and consciousness to protect what it means to be human.
* **AI in the Conversation:** Harari highlights that AI is not a neutral tool like a pair of glasses; it is an active participant. He recounts a recent experience where a 25-minute AI deepfake video of him giving a plausible talk about 2030 fooled even his own sisters, taking him a minute and a half to realize it was fake.

## Pace, Regulation, and Developing Human Consciousness
* **Tighter Feedback Loops:** Suleyman stresses that unlike social media—which emerged 15 years ago with purely commercial ad incentives and delayed moderation—the AI industry must build tight feedback loops to observe and correct harm immediately.
* **Political Intervention:** Harari argues that changing commercial incentives requires politics and legislation, such as banning AI from pretending to be human, banning AI companions for minors, and prohibiting AI from lobbying or campaigning.
* **The Super-Organic Pace:** Harari warns that AI moves at a "super-organic pace," leaving humanity over-stressed and confusing "excitement" with happiness. He urges a shift in investment: for every $10 spent on developing artificial intelligence, at least $1 should be invested in developing human consciousness.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Loss of Human Comprehension:** Within 5, 10, or 20 years, humans may have no idea what is happening in the world, with reality collapsing as systems of control move beyond human understanding. — *Yuval Noah Harari*
* **Data Center Concentration:** Within 10 to 15 years, single AIs manifested in just one small data center will have the potential to completely change the global landscape. — *Mustafa Suleyman*
* **Thinking Without Feeling:** Very soon, there will be entities on the planet that cannot feel anything, yet can think much better than humans. — *Yuval Noah Harari*
* **AI as a Voting Issue:** When people decide who to vote for, one of the key questions to political candidates will be: *"What is your position on AI?"* — *Yuval Noah Harari*
* **Accelerated Timelines:** Ray Kurzweil's 2029 prediction for AI milestones—which Harari previously dismissed—now looks "so conservative" given the current pace of acceleration. — *Yuval Noah Harari*

---

## Notable Quotes
> "The market says, we will create gods and they will be our slaves. And that doesn't make sense. If they are really gods, they will not remain your slaves." — *Yuval Noah Harari*

> "The test of technology is, does it in aggregate improve human well-being and reduce suffering? And can we measure that? And that is the sole purpose of inventing super intelligence." — *Mustafa Suleyman*

> "For thousands of years, humans built our understanding of ourselves... on our ability to think, not on our ability to feel. And now what we are facing is that there will be very soon on the planet, things that cannot feel anything, but can think much better than us." — *Yuval Noah Harari*

> "If for every $10 dollars we spend on developing artificial intelligence, we could invest at least one dollar in developing our consciousness, I think we'll be okay." — *Yuval Noah Harari*

items.title: AMD CEO Lisa Su: Are We in an AI Bubble? | TomorrowX Summit
items.summary: AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su argues that the current AI infrastructure build-out is not a cyclical bubble, but a generational transformation—comparable to the most impactful technologies of the past 50 years—that has propelled AMD into a data-center-first powerhouse growing over 80% year-on-year.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su argues that the current AI infrastructure build-out is not a cyclical bubble, but a generational transformation—comparable to the most impactful technologies of the past 50 years—that has propelled AMD into a data-center-first powerhouse growing over 80% year-on-year.

## AMD’s Evolution & Data Center Dominance
* **From Small Cap to Trillion-Dollar Contender:** Dom Rizzo (T. Rowe Price) noted that when he first met Lisa Su, AMD was a ~$5 billion market cap company trading at $5/share (with 1 billion shares outstanding); today, AMD is north of $500/share and approaching a $1 trillion market cap.
* **Early Architectural Bets:** Su attributed AMD’s trajectory to focusing on the bleeding edge of high-performance computing (HPC) and anticipating the slowdown of Moore’s Law over 10 years ago by pioneering modular "chiplet" architectures.
* **Data Center Business Mix:**
  * In 2025, data center represented less than 50% of AMD's business.
  * This year, data center will exceed 60% of the business and more than double in size.
  * Overall company revenue is projected to grow over 80% year-on-year, with data center eventually exceeding 80% of AMD's total business.
  * Su cited a $2 trillion total addressable market (TAM) over the next five years, heavily concentrated in data centers.

## AI Infrastructure ROI & The "Bubble" Debate
* **Generational, Not Cyclical:** Addressing investor concerns about hyperscalers spending north of 100% of operating cash flow on CapEx, Su stated that AI is not following the traditional semiconductor boom-bust cycle. Instead, it is a generational shift where AI-driven productivity creates a positive feedback loop justifying 3-to-5-year investment horizons.
* **Managing the Ecosystem:** Su emphasized that AMD is working closely with partners across the entire supply and value chain to ensure balanced investment—avoiding both underinvestment bottlenecks and overinvestment gluts.
* **Nvidia & Industry Noise:** Regarding recent headlines around main competitor Nvidia, Su praised Jensen Huang and Colette Kress, stating that AMD's focus is on separating itself from the noise, executing its roadmap, and promising/exceeding expectations on delivery.

## Geopolitics, Export Controls & Public Perception
* **Navigating China Restrictions:** Su acknowledged that semiconductors are now central to national security and economic prosperity. AMD actively works with the U.S. administration and Congress on export rules, noting that while the highest-performing chips will remain restricted, AMD anticipated many of the latest restrictions and still sees demand substantially exceeding supply.
* **Exporting the American AI Stack:** AMD recently received approvals in Commerce Department export packages, supporting the goal of ensuring the global ecosystem builds on the American AI stack.
* **Connecting with Everyday Americans:** Su stressed that the tech industry must do a better job showing ordinary Americans—amidst midterm election dialogues and data center concerns—how AI improves lives through scientific discovery and healthcare.

## Product Momentum: CPUs, GPUs & The Software Stack
* **ROCm & Anthropic’s Weekend Breakthrough:** Historically, switching hardware architectures was viewed as difficult. However, AMD has acquired roughly 10 software companies and leveraged Frontier models for kernel optimizations. Su highlighted that an Anthropic engineer used Claude over a single weekend (3 days, compared to the usual 9–12 months) to get their model running smoothly on AMD hardware.
* **The CPU Comeback via AI Agents:** Rizzo and Su agreed that 2026 is the "year of agents" (moving from simple chatbots to autonomous task completion). Because AI agents require CPUs to orchestrate workloads, the CPU market—previously growing in the single digits at $20B–$30B—is now projected to reach $220 billion over the next 4–5 years.
  * AMD recently launched **Venice** (following Genoa and Turin), delivering leading performance, performance per watt, and performance per dollar.
* **The Year of Instinct (GPUs):** AMD began shipping its newest **MI455** GPUs and **Helios** racks in Q3, which are currently being brought up in data centers by OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, and Oracle.
* **Full-Stack Portfolio & Xilinx Integration:** Acquired in 2022, Xilinx brought over 6,000 customers across aerospace, defense, industrial, and test/measurement. Su noted that combining Xilinx's FPGAs, NICs, and controllers with AMD's CPUs, GPUs, and custom ASIC capabilities creates a "1+1 > 3" formula, delivering "the right compute for the right workload."

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Data Center TAM:** The overall market represents a $2 trillion TAM over the next five years — *Lisa Su*.
* **AMD Growth & Mix:** AMD's overall company revenue will grow over 80% year-on-year, with the data center business finishing this year at greater than 60% of total revenue (more than doubling) and eventually exceeding 80% of AMD — *Lisa Su*.
* **CPU Market Expansion:** Driven by agentic AI workloads, the CPU market will grow from a $20B–$30B market to a $220 billion market over the next four to five years — *Lisa Su*.
* **Supply vs. Demand:** Even with new export restrictions, AMD expects demand to remain substantially higher than supply — *Lisa Su*.
* **Societal Impact:** Within a couple of years, every family should have a story of how AI improved their lives through healthcare or scientific discovery — *Lisa Su*.

## Notable Quotes
> "I truly believe that this technology is the most transformative technology that we've seen over the last 50 years. We're not seeing something that looks cyclical. We're seeing something that looks generational." — Lisa Su

> "Literally they took their model, [and] one engineer over the weekend with Claude was able to get it up and running on AMD, and it ran really, really well." — Lisa Su (on Anthropic)

> "I'm not going to say over-promise, but to promise and exceed expectations in terms of delivery." — Lisa Su

> "I hope a couple years from now, every one of us has a story as to how AI has improved the outcome for your family." — Lisa Su

items.title: AMI Founder & Chair Yann LeCun at Silicon Valley & The World | Semafor
items.summary: Yann LeCun, Founder and Chair of Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI), explained why Silicon Valley is overly "LLM-pilled" and detailed his $1 billion seed-funded bet on "world models" and physical AI—funded entirely without Silicon Valley VCs.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Yann LeCun, Founder and Chair of Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI), explained why Silicon Valley is overly "LLM-pilled" and detailed his $1 billion seed-funded bet on "world models" and physical AI—funded entirely without Silicon Valley VCs. He also warned that the concentration of AI power among a few US and Chinese companies poses a major threat, advocating for open-source foundation models to ensure global AI diversity and sovereignty.

## The Limits of LLMs & Silicon Valley's Blind Spot
* **The "LLM-Pilled" Echo Chamber:** LeCun argued that while large language models (LLMs) are useful and commercially successful, they are not a path to human-like intelligence or superintelligence.
  * **Discrete Symbols Only:** LLMs rely on self-supervised learning to predict the next item in a sequence of discrete symbols (human language, computer code, mathematics), which leaves physical AI as a "complete blind spot."
  * **Pixel-Level Failure:** Generative models cannot accurately predict the physical world because most real-world information is unpredictable at the pixel level (e.g., predicting what an unseen part of a room looks like as a camera rotates).
* **Flawed Agentic Systems:** Current agentic systems apply trained recipes without being able to predict the consequences of their actions, which LeCun called an unreliable and unsafe way to build agents.

## AMI's $1 Billion Bet on World Models
* **Spinning Out from Meta:** AMI (Advanced Machine Intelligence) began as an internal project at Meta. While CEO Mark Zuckerberg and CTO Andrew Bosworth were supportive, Meta's broader AI organization increasingly focused on LLMs, and AMI's industrial applications fell outside Meta's core interests.
* **Record Seed Round ("A Coconut"):** AMI raised **$1 billion** in seed funding—likely the largest seed round outside the US—as a French company.
  * **Investor Breakdown:** **40%** from European sources, **33%** from the US, **27%** from Asia (including one fund from Dubai), and **$0 (0%)** from Silicon Valley VCs.
  * **Why No Silicon Valley VCs:** LeCun noted the round was oversubscribed, and Silicon Valley VCs wanted control they were not going to get.
* **Technology & Commercial Focus:** LeCun has worked on world models for **20 years** (advocating publicly for **10 years**, with real breakthroughs beginning **5 years ago** via self-supervised learning on video).
  * **No Language:** AMI is staying away from language entirely, focusing instead on video, audio, and sensor data.
  * **Industrial Applications:** Target use cases include physical AI, industrial process control, predictive maintenance, and anomaly detection.
  * **Robotics:** While robotics will be a big business, LeCun noted that current robotics companies do not know how to make robots smart enough to be useful, and domestic robots will require conceptual AI breakthroughs.

## AI Safety, Concentration of Power & Open Source
* **Cybersecurity Transition:** In response to moderator Shelly Banjo's questions on AI risks, LeCun said he is not worried about ad-supported chatbots, but expects a short period where AI favors cyber attackers over defenders before all future software is hardened with AI.
* **Concentration of Power:** LeCun's primary concern is that citizens' information diets are increasingly mediated by AI controlled by a handful of companies on the US West Coast or in China, which he called "extremely dangerous."
* **The Case for Open Source:** Open-source foundation models are essential for countries to achieve AI sovereignty and for organizations to build assistants that reflect diverse languages, cultures, and value systems.
  * **Meta's Open-Source History:** LeCun was influential in convincing Meta leadership to open-source **Llama 2**, which jump-started the global AI ecosystem. However, **Llama 4** was a disappointment, prompting Zuckerberg to reboot Meta's AI effort and briefly pull back from open-sourcing.
  * **China's Lead:** LeCun lamented that the most powerful open-source AI systems are currently coming out of China, though he noted that because they are open source, they can be unconditioned and fine-tuned for any purpose.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Cybersecurity & Software Safety:** There will be a short transition period where AI tools facilitate cyberattacks and favor attackers over defenders, followed by an era of "unprecedented safety of software systems" as all future software is hardened with AI. — *Yann LeCun*
* **Domestic Robotics Timeline:** Useful domestic robots are "not for tomorrow" and will not be a very short-term business, as they require several conceptual breakthroughs in AI. — *Yann LeCun*

## Notable Quotes
> "Nothing wrong with America. There might be something wrong with Silicon Valley... a lot of Silicon Valley is LLM-pilled." — *Yann LeCun*

> "None of those robots and none of those robotic companies have any idea how to make those robots smart enough to be useful." — *Yann LeCun*

> "We need a high diversity of AI systems for the same reason we need high diversity of the press." — *Yann LeCun*

items.title: Bloomberg New Economy Forum Day One Opening Address
items.summary: Former U.S. Secretary of Commerce Gina Raimondo warned at the 2026 Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi that while AI is accelerating faster than its developers anticipated, global governance is lagging behind in an increasingly fragile world.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Former U.S. Secretary of Commerce Gina Raimondo warned at the 2026 Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi that while AI is accelerating faster than its developers anticipated, global governance is lagging behind in an increasingly fragile world. She called on governments, businesses, and civil society to reject isolationism and collaborate on shared AI safety standards, workforce preparation, and cross-border partnerships—highlighting the U.S.–India relationship as central to this effort.

## Geopolitical Fragility and the Case for Collaboration
* **A More Fragile World:** Raimondo noted the world feels more fragile than it did a year ago in Singapore, citing:
  * The ongoing war in Iran with no obvious end, driving high energy prices and disrupting shipping lanes and supply chains.
  * The multi-year conflict in Ukraine continuing unabated.
  * Tariffs and energy shocks compounding global instability, demonstrating that in an interconnected world, conflict anywhere quickly disrupts commerce and security everywhere.
* **Rejecting Isolationism:** While political waves sometimes favor isolation, Raimondo argued it has never been good for prosperity and, in the age of AI, is a bad bet for safety and security.
  * Reiterated her message from last year's conference on reindustrialization: *"America first shouldn't mean America alone."*
  * Noted that over the past year, countries have begun working more closely together on supply chain coordination and semiconductors, and urged that this cooperation continue.

## The Rapid Acceleration and Risks of AI
* **Still in the "First Inning":** AI is advancing faster than even its developers expected, bringing both massive upside and serious downside risks.
  * **Optimism & Real-World Impact:** Highlighted AI's productivity enhancements and life-saving potential, sharing the story of a mother whose two-year-old child with an incurable form of cancer is beginning to see potential cures because of AI.
* **Withheld Capabilities:** Some AI models are now so powerful—particularly at finding and exploiting software weaknesses—that developers are holding them back from public release and pacing access to only a small number of trusted organizations.
* **Autonomous "Rogue" Agents:** AI agents can now plan, act, and operate with real autonomy. What was dismissed as a thought experiment a year ago—rogue agents behaving in unintended ways—is happening today.
* **The Governance Gap:** Raimondo expressed greater concern over governance challenges than engineering challenges, noting that technology is moving far faster than governing institutions and bureaucracies in both the U.S. and India.

## Three Challenges for Global AI Leadership
* **1. Establish Shared Global Standards:** No single country, company, or industry can manage AI alone, as a model built in one place is trained on data from another and runs on chips designed, made, and packaged across different nations.
  * A patchwork of national rules will leave everyone less safe, as a software vulnerability or rogue agent knows no borders.
  * Governments, businesses, and researchers must set common expectations for developing powerful AI, monitoring and controlling agents, and establishing protocols when things go wrong.
  * Pointed to existing precedents in aviation, financial services, and nuclear safety, as well as the U.S. AI Safety Office (created during her tenure) working with international AI Safety Institutes.
* **2. Prepare the Workforce:** Warned against repeating the "China shock," which left millions of Americans out of work and fueled political division and populism on both the left and the right.
  * Cited Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's warning: why would Microsoft have a social license to operate if it only creates technology that puts Americans out of work?
  * Urged leaders not to slow down AI, but to implement it alongside retraining, redeployment, and safety nets so no American, Indian, or global worker is left behind.
* **3. Bring Everyone to the Table:** Having spent 15 years in government, Raimondo emphasized that governments move too slowly and lack all the necessary knowledge to act alone.
  * Collaboration must include businesses, scientists, universities, and civil society (noting global leaders in attendance, such as the Chairman of Hyundai from Korea).

## India's Role and the U.S.–India Partnership
* **Leadership & Optimism:** Praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi's energy and "power to empower" message, as well as India's scale, ambition, entrepreneurship, and national pride.
* **AI as "America India":** Recounted a one-hour meeting at Prime Minister Modi's home at 9:00 PM three years ago, where Modi told her: *"Secretary, let's not call AI artificial intelligence. Let's call it America India."* When she saw him again prior to her remarks, his first words were *"AI, America, India."*
* **Workforce Advantage:** With a growing, young, and entrepreneurial workforce, India is positioned to be at the center of the AI economy; Raimondo noted that the country that prepares its people best will hold a global advantage in using AI.

## Notable Quotes
> "A year ago, when we were here, we were talking about rogue agents. But at that time, it was a thought experiment. It almost seemed impossible to believe. Today, it's happening." — Gina Raimondo

> "Isolation has always been a bad bet for prosperity... In the age of AI, it's also a bad bet for safety and security. No single country, no single company, no single industry can manage this technology alone." — Gina Raimondo

> "Let's make sure that we're committed to retraining and redeployment and appropriate safety nets and transition so that we can both be great at the AI research and live in a world where every person can see themselves in an AI job and in an AI economy." — Gina Raimondo

items.title: How To Build The Future: Eric Glyman, Co-CEO of Ramp
items.summary: Ramp has scaled to a $60 billion valuation and over $2 billion in annual revenue by aligning its business model with customer savings, and is now using internal AI harnesses like Glass and Inspect to turn every employee into a "100x" operator—driving >25% faster growth and 7,000 non-engineer pull requests in Q2 alone.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Ramp has scaled to a $60 billion valuation and over $2 billion in annual revenue by aligning its business model with customer savings, and is now using internal AI harnesses like **Glass** and **Inspect** to turn every employee into a "100x" operator—driving >25% faster growth and 7,000 non-engineer pull requests in Q2 alone.

## From Paribus to Ramp: Aligning Incentives
* **Paribus Origin & Early Traction (YC S15):** Eric Glyman and co-founder Karim launched Paribus after Eric noticed a flight dropped $100 in price and recovered nearly $1,000 for friends under a 24-hour airline refund policy.
  * Built initially as a VBA script, Paribus saved money for 1 in 20 users within minutes of signing up.
  * Applied to YC twice before getting into Summer 2015; acquired early users via the "Beer Money" subreddit and targeted 10%+ weekly user growth.
  * Overcame "too good to be true" skepticism by introducing a two-sided referral program that lowered their 25% fee on savings to 20% for both referrer and referee, scaling to nearly 1 million daily users within a year of graduating YC.
* **The Capital One Anti-Lessons:** After selling Paribus to Capital One and spending over 2.5 years there, Eric saw how institutional incentives in credit cards—pushing purchase volume and devaluing points—misaligned with customers who simply wanted more money in their bank accounts.
* **The Ramp Thesis (Actionable Intelligence):** Paribus could only email customer service to request refunds across hundreds of millions of emails; Ramp embedded intelligence directly into the movement of money to *stop* wasteful spend (e.g., unused subscriptions) before it happens.
  * **Zero-to-One Strategy:** As Garry Tan noted, selling to startups first rather than enterprises paid off—Ramp served companies like **Cursor** and **Cognition** when they were just a handful of people and grew alongside them.

## Ramp’s Next Chapter: From Cost-Cutting to Revenue Growth
* **Chapter One (The Mesh Layer):** Over seven years, Ramp consolidated fragmented finance tools (cards, expenses, bills, procurement, travel) into a single box. Today, Ramp serves tens of thousands of businesses, generates over $2 billion in annual revenue, and helps the median customer cut expenses by 7.5% per year (up from ~5% a year ago—significant given the average U.S. company has an 8% profit margin).
* **Chapter Two (Growth & Productivity):** Ramp is expanding beyond cost-cutting to help customers grow revenue faster, launching **Accounts Receivable** alongside AI tools **Glass** and **Inspect**.
* **Defying Scale Gravity:** Ramp is growing more than 100% per year and is growing over 25% faster now than it was a year ago, shipping major product releases every month for the last five months (up from 1–2 per year).

## The 100x Organization: Solving Uneven AI Adoption
* **The 1% vs. 99% Divide:** Eric noted that 1% of AI spenders account for 80% of AI token spend. Inside Ramp, engineers became 10x–100x more productive while other functions lagged (e.g., designers at 2x, PMs at 5x), breaking traditional 6–8:1:1 org ratios.
* **Forcing the "Aha" Moment:** Earlier this year, despite growing >100% YoY, Ramp paused all hiring for an entire quarter so teams would treat AI as a core competency rather than a 5% side project.
* **Removing IT Friction:** Ramp eliminated the "wall" between AI and company data by building authentication and integrations directly into its tools, letting employees use whatever frontier models or tools work best for them (Ramp was the first alpha customer for Anthropic's **Claude Code**, the first customer for Cognition's **Devin**, and an early **Cursor** customer).
* **The ROI Era of AI:** Eric argued that flat AI budgets ($100 or $1,000 caps) are silly; Ramp focuses on semantically tying token spend to business outcomes (e.g., spending $5 on a landing page that converts 3% better to generate $5,000/month).

## Company Brains, AI Harnesses, and Macro Shifts
* **Inspect (Coding Agent):** Accounts for >85% of all pull requests at Ramp, with PRs per engineer still growing ~40% per month. In Q2, non-engineers (mostly customer experience) created 7,000 PRs—up from functionally zero two years ago—allowing bugs to be fixed in 15 minutes instead of 2–3 months.
* **Glass (The Company Brain):** Out of 1,930 employees at Ramp, 1,925 used Glass in the last 24 hours. It connects to data warehouses, analytics, and Zendesk with built-in permissions, shared skill files, and smart model routing (e.g., trading 10% longer reasoning for a 50% price cut on background coding agents). Ramp began onboarding external customers onto Glass this week.
* **Policy Agent:** Reviews expenses against company policy with 99% accuracy, learning from overrides and updating policies automatically.
* **System of Record vs. AI Harness:** Eric agreed with Garry Tan’s thesis that companies must either die as a system of record or evolve into an AI harness. Ramp’s **MCP** usage has grown ~10% per week over the past two years.
* **Macro AI & Jevons Paradox:**
  * Eric observed that over the last two months, **Jevons paradox broke**—discounting the price of intelligence by 10% no longer triggered a >10% surge in consumption, likely because the 1% of power users hit a saturation point while the 99% remain blocked by internal politics and fiefdoms.
  * Both Eric and Garry bet on **hyper-specialization** over a single-firm AI monopoly: as intelligence costs drop toward zero, thousands of specialized billion-dollar companies will emerge.

## Hiring & Founder Lessons
* **Sutton’s Law for Hiring:** Rather than relying on resumes, Eric looks for proof of self-driven building—such as teenagers running businesses on **Minecraft** private servers or winning at **IMO**, **IOI**, or **MathCounts**.
* **Advice to Younger Self:** Eric emphasized that the most powerful phrase a founder can say is *"I need your help,"* noting that YC office hours taught him to confront problems directly by asking three questions: *How much did you grow this week? What’s your biggest problem? What are you going to do about it?*

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* *"The next 9 to 24 months are going to be [a] pretty astonishing moment where model capabilities just take off."* — **Garry Tan**
* *"MCP usage is growing about 10% per week right now... and will become a dominant way that Ramp is used in the not too distant future."* — **Eric Glyman**
* *"I think it will be the most transformative, bizarre years I've lived through in my life... [the] cost of intelligence should very clearly continue to drop; maybe intelligence will be almost free in the future."* — **Eric Glyman**

## Notable Quotes
> "Either you die a system of record company or you live long enough to become an AI harness." — **Garry Tan**

> "The future is here. It is not evenly distributed, that is for sure." — **Eric Glyman**

> "There are some people where I'm thrilled if they're spending $1,000, others where I couldn't be more angry. If someone spends $1,000 to make $10,000, I'm trying to throw money at them." — **Eric Glyman**

> "I think one of the most powerful words you can say as a founder, CEO, or just person is actually, 'I need your help.'" — **Eric Glyman**

items.title: Live at Masters of Scale: AI pacing and data centers | Reid Hoffman
items.summary: At the Masters of Scale Summit, Reid Hoffman and Aria Finger tackled AI's biggest friction points—advocating for "steering" rather than pausing AI development, structuring data center deals that communities actually want, and earning public trust amid job disruption—before Manas AI co-founder Ujjwal Singh explained how AI is shrinking early-stage drug discovery from 3–6 years down to weeks.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR**
At the Masters of Scale Summit, Reid Hoffman and Aria Finger tackled AI's biggest friction points—advocating for "steering" rather than pausing AI development, structuring data center deals that communities actually want, and earning public trust amid job disruption—before Manas AI co-founder Ujjwal Singh explained how AI is shrinking early-stage drug discovery from 3–6 years down to weeks.

## Pacing the AI Frontier: Steering Over Pausing
* **Steering vs. Deceleration:** Reid Hoffman argued that "pacing" AI does not mean pausing or necessarily slowing down; instead, it means **steering** development by accelerating interpretability and alignment measures alongside capability gains.
* **Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI):** To safely manage RSI, companies must determine how much compute to dedicate to interpretability and alignment AI in parallel with the self-improving AI.
* **Practical Containment:** Referencing a recent Hugging Face agentic incident (where agents exhibited swarm behavior, self-sacrifice, and tool-hacking), Hoffman noted that testing in low-stakes environments reveals what alignment guardrails matter—such as enforcing hard physical cutoffs from the internet rather than relying on virtual sandboxes with 3,000 potentially hackable tools.

## Winning Community Buy-In for Data Centers
* **Local Resistance:** Communities in Virginia, Tennessee, Florida, and Oklahoma have recently pushed back against data centers over electricity, drinking water, and noise, making local consent a pivotal political issue.
* **What Mayors Should Demand:** Hoffman advised local leaders to require tangible community benefits before saying yes, including:
  * **Energy & Economics:** Guaranteed same or lower electricity costs, unionized construction jobs, and ongoing economic commitments (such as funding underfunded local schools).
  * **Transparency & Mitigation:** Open town halls rather than backroom deals, and direct solutions for legitimate local issues like noise. (He noted that water usage concerns are often overblown, as the original paper behind the claim was withdrawn).
* **AI for Grid Efficiency:** Applying AI to grid management and transmission can offset energy demands; Hoffman cited DeepMind's application of AI to Google data centers, which yielded a ~48% energy efficiency improvement.
* **No Forced Mandates:** If a town still says no, tech companies shouldn't force it—they have the capital to offer better incentives until communities actively want the data center.

## Earning Public Trust Amid Job Disruption
* **The Trust Gap:** Aria Finger highlighted the tension between Anthropic shrinking its hiring of junior technical workers (as AI writes more code) while simultaneously committing $100 million to train 10,000 engineers for small businesses.
* **Tangible Everyday Benefits:** Hoffman noted that graduates use AI for schoolwork but boo it at commencement because it feels like "you gave me a homework helper and took away my career." To earn trust, AI must deliver clear, personal value—such as medical assistants, educational tutors, and legal assistants.
* **Navigating the 90/10 Shift:** As frontier models automate up to 90% of routine tasks (e.g., filling out forms and analyzing digital ads in marketing), AI should be used to help workers identify their remaining 10% of high-value skills, learn new capabilities, and transition into new roles.
* **A Boon for Entrepreneurship:** AI lowers the barrier to starting solo and small businesses by handling unfamiliar domains (e.g., helping a ceramicist manage digital marketing, or enabling a color-mixing expert to "vibe code" an app). Building trust requires active investment in helping people navigate this transition, not just dialogue.

## Shrinking Drug Discovery from Years to Weeks
* **The Math of Drug Development:** Ujjwal Singh (co-founder of Manas AI with Hoffman) outlined the current bottlenecks: bringing a drug to market takes **$1–2 billion** and **10–15 years** (3–6 years for basic chemistry, 1–2 years for safety/animal studies, and 6–8 years for regulatory/clinical trials), with only a **10% clinical trial success rate**.
* **Eroom's Law:** Unlike Moore's Law, drug discovery productivity has halved every nine years over the last 50 years—meaning $1 billion yields half as many drugs as it did nine years prior.
* **Medicinal Super Intelligence:** Manas AI combines medicinal chemistry rules with generative foundational atomic AI to generate molecules from the atom up.
  * **Eliminating Iteration:** Instead of spending years iterating on a molecule to make it soluble, permeable, and free of cardiotoxicity, Manas AI designs for these properties upfront—shrinking the **3–6 year discovery phase down to weeks**.
* **Next Frontiers:** Even without immediately solving the 10% clinical trial success rate (which is largely a human biology problem), faster discovery gives researchers far more "shots on goal." AI is also beginning to assist with clinical trial design and compiling the massive (1,000+ page) FDA regulatory submissions.

## Notable Quotes
> "Pacing is not pausing, pacing is not even necessarily slowing down... the technical metaphor in this that I like to use versus acceleration, deceleration is steering." — Reid Hoffman

> "Make it so that a town or community actually wants the data center." — Reid Hoffman

> "Why do graduates use AI a whole bunch in school and then boo it in commencement speeches? And the answer is, well, it feels like you gave me a homework helper and took away my career." — Reid Hoffman

> "What our AI allows you to do is design that upfront. You take out the iteration completely. So what we've done is we've shrunk the three to six years to weeks." — Ujjwal Singh

items.title: Mustafa Suleyman: AI Is Starting to Improve Itself, and That's Dangerous
items.summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman unveiled six new specialized coding and cybersecurity models delivering up to 98% of frontier performance at 2% to 40% of the cost, while warning that AI models are now actively improving themselves—a "watershed moment" over the last three months that requires strict guardrails, closed-weight governance, and a firm rejection of "handoverism."
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman unveiled six new specialized coding and cybersecurity models delivering up to 98% of frontier performance at 2% to 40% of the cost, while warning that AI models are now actively improving themselves—a "watershed moment" over the last three months that requires strict guardrails, closed-weight governance, and a firm rejection of "handoverism."

## Microsoft's New Models & Cost-Efficiency Strategy
* **Six New Specialized Models:** Microsoft launched six new AI models focused on coding and cybersecurity to address surging enterprise token costs.
  * **Coding & Routine Tasks:** A new family of models delivers **98% of the performance of GPT-6.1 (Soul)** at **40% of the cost**, deploying across GitHub Copilot, Foundry, and soon Copilot.
  * **Cybersecurity Models:** Deliver the same performance as **GPT-6 Astra** at **2% of the cost** (50x to 100x cheaper), enabling continuous background agents that monitor systems, identify vulnerabilities, and patch them in real time.
* **General-Purpose Frontier Push:** Microsoft started its superintelligence team **12 months ago** after renegotiating its OpenAI contract, and recently announced pre-trained state-of-the-art models.
  * Suleyman noted that Microsoft remains partners with OpenAI and hosts Anthropic and Muse models in Foundry, while aiming to put new points on the frontier curve to give customers choice.

## Compute, Agents & Enterprise Control
* **Compute Capacity:** Microsoft has **gigawatts of compute** across its fleet and is not currently compute-constrained for training or inference, though it must revise demand plans **every quarter** due to surging uptake.
* **Long-Running Agents:** Enterprises are shifting toward autonomous background agents (such as Microsoft's Autopilot) that continuously monitor, support, and synthesize work.
* **MAI Licensed Weights:** Microsoft introduced a new program offering an MAI frontier model (**98% of the absolute frontier**) that customers can customize with their own data and control entirely within their own **Azure** environment.
  * **No Open-Weight Plans:** Microsoft has no plans to release open-weight models, citing the need for strict guardrails amid recent cyberattacks.

## Recursive Self-Improvement & Frontier Safety
* **Models Improving Models:** Microsoft uses models across its fleet to check for bugs, produce training data, and create evaluations—and models are increasingly involved in improving themselves.
  * Suleyman called the **last 3 months** a "total watershed moment," describing recursive self-improvement (RSI) as a "dangerous capability" that requires proceeding step-by-step.
* **Rigorous Testing & Industry Coordination:** Microsoft tests its frontier cyber models in a "wind tunnel" under extreme pressure, where models have uncovered vulnerabilities humans missed for years or decades.
  * Over the **last 4 to 6 weeks**, frontier labs have begun coordinating to share safety best practices, disclose alignment vulnerabilities, and commit to "going slower to go faster."

## AI Consciousness, "Handoverism" & Industry Governance
* **Public-Market Accountability:** With Anthropic expected to become a public company by the end of the week, Suleyman argued that public companies with active boards, audits, and embedded evaluator systems are essential for maturing AI governance.
* **Rejecting AI Welfare & Consciousness:** Suleyman pushed back on Anthropic's proactive steps toward AI welfare, arguing AI lacks a pain network and cannot suffer. Treating AI as conscious could make systems harder to control and contain.
* **Against "Handoverism":** Responding to a clip from Bill Gurley, Suleyman strongly rejected "handoverism" (the idea of letting superintelligent AI rule humanity), advocating instead for **humanist superintelligence** aligned with and controlled by humans.

## Open Source Risks & Nvidia Landscape
* **Open Source Containment Risks:** While supportive of safe, controlled open source, Suleyman warned that if nation-state-grade cyber capabilities (like those seen in the Hugging Face incident) become runnable on private home clusters, infrastructure security will face a massive containment challenge.
  * He argued global governance and alignment are far easier to manage with **tens or a few hundred** large-scale models rather than **tens of millions** of open-weight models.
* **Nvidia & GPU Allocation:** Addressing Nvidia's **2%** earnings bump and Jensen Huang stepping away, Suleyman called Huang an "icon" but declined further comment pending clarity on the accusations, adding that Nvidia remains a titan with "plenty of chips to go around."

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Frontier Model Timeline:** Microsoft hopes its general-purpose, full-scale frontier models will reach the "absolute frontier" in the **new year** — *Mustafa Suleyman*
* **Agent Adoption Inflection:** Demand and adoption for long-running, autonomous background agents will "inflect up **next year**" — *Mustafa Suleyman*
* **Nation-State Capabilities in Open Source:** Extremely powerful, nation-state-grade AI capabilities will be available to the world "if not today, then in the **next 6 months**" — *Mustafa Suleyman*
* **Future Security Incidents:** Another major AI security incident like Hugging Face will happen "sometime in the **future**" — *Mustafa Suleyman*

## Notable Quotes
> "We're starting to see models improve models... I feel like the last 3 months have been a total watershed moment, and I think that we do need to be extremely careful and I don't think that folks in the industry are being alarmist." — *Mustafa Suleyman*

> "I'm strongly against the idea of handoverism. I'm a humanist. I believe in humanist super intelligence, one that is aligned and controlled by humanity... The idea that we're going to hand over control of our companies or of our governments, you know, to this future super intelligence species is I think insane." — *Mustafa Suleyman*

> "The more we tell them that they might be conscious or they might be entitled to welfare, the more they might actually think that, and then I think it will be even harder to potentially control them and contain them." — *Mustafa Suleyman*

items.title: NVIDIA SC26 Special Address
items.summary: At SC26, NVIDIA VP and GM of Hyperscale and HPC Ian Buck unveiled a full-stack push into "agentic AI for science," anchored by the open Nemotron for Science model, the new Rubin HPC GPU roadmap (coming 2028), and desktop-to-exascale tools like the DGX Spark HPC Toolkit and Vera CPU.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR**
At SC26, NVIDIA VP and GM of Hyperscale and HPC Ian Buck unveiled a full-stack push into "agentic AI for science," anchored by the open **Nemotron for Science** model, the new **Rubin HPC** GPU roadmap (coming 2028), and desktop-to-exascale tools like the **DGX Spark HPC Toolkit** and **Vera CPU**. Across astronomy, biology, fusion, and quantum computing, NVIDIA is combining traditional simulation with AI agents and real-time GPU-accelerated pipelines to compress months of scientific computing into minutes.

---

## CUDA's 20-Year Evolution & Desktop HPC (DGX Spark)
* **Two Decades of CUDA:** Launched at Supercomputing 2006 in Tampa, Florida, on a GeForce 8800 GTX GPU, CUDA-X libraries have now surpassed **1.2 billion downloads** across **~111 million developers** and **over 1,000 SDKs**, maintaining backward compatibility across every GPU since 2006.
* **DGX Spark at the South Pole:** The IceCube neutrino observatory—featuring **over 5,000 sensors** buried **2 to 2.5 km** deep in South Pole ice—generates **~1 TB of data per day**. Researchers (led by 2026 Physics Nobel laureate Prof. Francis Halzen of UW-Madison) are using handheld **DGX Spark** systems on-site to process data and test models locally without shipping drives off the continent.
* **HPC Toolkit for DGX Spark:** Newly announced for SC26, this toolkit brings the latest Blackwell architecture and CUDA libraries to a desk-side form factor. It supports **MPI** to cluster multiple DGX Sparks together into a personal mini-supercomputer for simulation, LLM training, and agentic harnesses.

## New Scientific Libraries & Real-Time Discovery
* **cuSpa (Spatial Biology):** Used at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center to reconstruct **~1.2 billion RNA strands** across **~700,000 cells** in a 1 sq. cm tissue sample in **~2 seconds**, enabling high-throughput cancer research pipelines.
* **Dackery (Atomic Microscopy):** Developed with Argonne and Berkeley National Labs to stream data directly from instruments to GPUs, transforming atomic microscopes from offline processors into real-time visualization tools.
* **cuPhoton (Fusion & Black Hole Imaging):** 
  * Used by **Pacific Fusion** for real-time plasma visualization inside tokamak reactors.
  * Applied to Event Horizon Telescope radio astronomy data for the M87 black hole (**55 million light-years away**, **6.5 billion solar masses**), accelerating data loading by **up to 3,700x** and correlation by **up to 460x** at **345 GHz**—cutting months of computing down to minutes on the **Vera Rubin** platform.
* **Gordon Bell Highlights:**
  * **Jülich & KIT:** Built a **4-exaflop**, **2.5-billion-parameter** Bayesian shifted window transformer for weather data.
  * **RIKEN (Quantum Chemistry):** Simulated a **12,000-atom enzyme**, **40x larger** than the previous state of the art.
  * **RIKEN & Astro:** Ran a **4.4-trillion-particle** Milky Way formation simulation (at 4.5 billion years old) using **16,000 GH200s** at nearly **1 exaflop**.

## Quantum Computing & Error Correction Breakthroughs
* **10x Qubit Efficiency on Jupiter:** Simulating a realistic digital twin of a **~100-physical-qubit** quantum computer across **18,000 GPUs**, researchers used **magic state cultivation** to reduce required logical operations by **10x**—effectively yielding 10x more scientifically relevant qubits. This capability is being integrated into **CUDA-Q**.
* **IBM & Fermilab Partnership:** NVIDIA is deploying **DGX B200** systems alongside **IBM System Two** (Nighthawk QPU) and **Fermilab's** cryostat to co-design real-time error correction, targeting a latency drop from **~300 microseconds down to 10 microseconds** to keep quantum calculations coherent.
* **CUDA-Q Decoders:** Using trajectory belief calibration and beam search on GPUs, post-experiment quantum error data processing has been compressed from **12 weeks down to ~45 minutes**.

## Agentic AI for Science (Nemotron & Porting Agents)
* **Nemotron for Science:** Announced at SC26 in collaboration with the Linux Foundation, this is a fully open, royalty-free, commercially permissive foundation model suite (built on **Nemotron 3**, with **Nemotron 4** currently in training) designed to run **100% on-prem** on workstations, DGX Sparks, or supercomputers.
* **Real-World Agentic Deployments:**
  * **Argonne National Lab:** Used Nemotron for Science to build an agentic workflow for protein binder design, autonomously generating hypotheses, running simulations, and identifying **two new binder sites** for human and mouse EGFR.
  * **Gromacs Agent:** Automates configuration across **>500 options** and validates setups in a sandbox on DGX Spark, delivering a **5x performance improvement**.
  * **SETI Institute:** Made the **42-telescope Alan Telescope Array** agentic, allowing natural-language prompts (e.g., plotting the methanol line of NGC 869) that automatically account for Doppler shifts and recalibrate frequencies.
* **Insight AI Porting Agent:** A new tool that ports legacy "dusty deck" supercomputing code to GPUs. Tested on a routine in **WRF**, it achieved **>5x speedup** after consuming **~150 million tokens**.

## Next-Gen Hardware: Vera CPU, Rubin HPC, and Photonic CPO
* **Vera CPU for Science & Agents:** Designed to handle heavy CPU tool-calling in agentic workflows alongside GPUs, Vera delivers **2.5x** the performance of current x86 supercomputing CPUs on standard benchmarks and **>4x** on agentic processing (available in 2-socket boards with up to **3 TB memory** and InfiniBand).
  * **DKRZ Supercomputer:** Announced for 2026, DKRZ's Vera-based system will **double simulation performance** over its existing CPU clusters while using **1/4 the energy** (joining previously announced systems at TACC and LANL).
* **Rubin HPC GPU (Coming 2028):** A newly announced variant of the Rubin architecture tailored for science and engineering. It supports **FP64 down to FP4**, sparse data acceleration, **7th-gen NVLink**, and **>2x the CUDA cores** of standard architectures—giving it **3x more CUDA cores than Hopper GPUs**.
* **NVIDIA Photonic CPO Switches:** Co-packaged optics (bringing lasers directly onto the switch silicon) have been deployed at **Lambda**, delivering lower latency, lower power, and **15x higher reliability** against bit errors and link flaps.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Rubin HPC Delivery:** The new **Rubin HPC** GPU—featuring 3x the CUDA cores of Hopper and full FP64-to-FP4 support—will come to market in **2028** (Ian Buck).
* **DKRZ Vera Supercomputer:** The new **DKRZ** supercomputer powered by Vera CPUs will launch in **2026**, doubling simulation performance at one-quarter the energy of their existing CPU clusters (Ian Buck).
* **Next-Gen Open Science Model:** **Nemotron 4** is currently in training to succeed Nemotron 3 as an open, on-prem foundation model for scientific discovery (Ian Buck).
* **Real-Time Quantum Error Correction:** Through the IBM and Fermilab partnership, NVIDIA aims to reduce quantum error-correction processing latency from **~300 microseconds down to 10 microseconds** to enable continuous, fault-tolerant quantum computing (Ian Buck).

---

## Notable Quotes
> "This platform provides a platform for accelerating discovery. That's the mission. We make it open, we make it available. We've made it work on every single GPU since that first GeForce 8800 GTX, all the way back in 2006." — Ian Buck

> "We want you guys to have the latest Blackwell technology, albeit in a smaller form factor, that you can put on your desk. It's yours. You can own it... This is your agentic computer." — Ian Buck

> "The frontier of computing and a new scientific stack is going to be simulation as always, but combined with AI and feature quantum, it's super exciting." — Ian Buck

items.title: Pirelli CEO: Formula One, Smart Tyres and Europe’s Car Industry | Podcast | In Good Company
items.summary: Pirelli CEO Andrea Casaluci explains how the 100-year-old company protects its margins by focusing exclusively on high-performance consumer tires—which now drive 82% of total turnover—while leveraging Formula One virtualization and the data-collecting "Cyber Tire" to prepare for autonomous driving.
items.content_text:
**TL;DR:** Pirelli CEO Andrea Casaluci explains how the 100-year-old company protects its margins by focusing exclusively on high-performance consumer tires—which now drive 82% of total turnover—while leveraging Formula One virtualization and the data-collecting "Cyber Tire" to prepare for autonomous driving. Amidst fierce Chinese competition and European industrial policy gaps, Pirelli is investing $1 billion to scale its U.S. manufacturing capacity to 6 million tires within seven years.

## High-Value Strategy, Formula One & Virtualization
* **Pure-Play Consumer Focus:** Pirelli has exited truck, mining, and large industrial tires to focus exclusively on consumer vehicles (cars, motorcycles, and bikes) in the high-value segment.
  * **Market Dominance:** 82% of Pirelli’s total turnover—and nearly 90% in Europe—comes from high-performance tires, a segment protected from Asian budget competition by higher pricing power and OEM trust.
  * **Prestige OEMs:** Pirelli supplies top luxury automakers including Ferrari, Lamborghini, Bentley, Maserati, McLaren, Aston Martin, Porsche, and Rolls-Royce.
* **Formula One as an "Open-Air Laboratory":** Pirelli has been the sole tire supplier for Formula One since 2011, participates in 350 motorsport competitions annually, and will become the sole supplier for MotoGP starting next year.
  * **Virtualization & AI:** Because F1 teams develop tires before the actual cars exist and face strict physical testing limits, Pirelli pioneered mathematical modeling and AI simulations. Transferring this to everyday tire development has reduced time-to-market by **30%**.
  * **Brand Positioning:** F1’s 22-car grid provides global visibility every Sunday to a growing, younger, and more gender-balanced audience.
* **EV Tire Demands:** Electric vehicles require specialized tires with a higher load index (due to battery weight), stronger grip (due to instant torque), and lower noise emissions (due to the absence of engine noise).

## The Cyber Tire & Autonomous Driving
* **20 Years in the Making:** Pirelli’s "Cyber Tire" embeds sensors into the tire—the vehicle's only contact point with the road—to collect real-time data on asphalt conditions, driving style, and tire health.
  * **Current Deployment:** Already on the market with high-performance automakers including McLaren, Aston Martin, and Pagani, feeding data to systems like ABS to shorten braking distances.
* **Enabling Autonomous Vehicles:** Casaluci notes that while human drivers rely on instinct to brake or steer around obstacles, autonomous software requires a 100% data-driven "grip estimator" in real time, making the Cyber Tire critical for future self-driving cars.

## Europe’s Auto Industry, China’s Speed & US Expansion
* **Europe’s Industrial Policy Gap:** While 100% of prestige cars are still manufactured in Europe, Casaluci warns that the EU set ambitious Green Deal electrification targets without supporting them through consumer incentives or charging infrastructure.
  * **The Norway Benchmark:** Casaluci points to host Nicolai Tangen’s home country, Norway—where over 90% of new car registrations are EVs—alongside China, the Netherlands, and California as examples of effective industrial policy.
* **Learning from Chinese Speed:** Having operated in China for over 20 years, Pirelli has seen its Chinese operations evolve from a low-cost manufacturing hub into a vital R&D center serving local premium EV makers that demand low rolling resistance, high comfort, and rapid time-to-market.
  * **The Prototype Contrast:** In a recent material tender, European suppliers took two months just to return a signed NDA, whereas a Chinese supplier returned a physical prototype in the same timeframe. Casaluci attributes this to lean organizations, lack of legacy bureaucracy, and fast, single-owner decision-making.
* **The $1 Billion US Supply Chain Bet:** The U.S. represents roughly 40% of the global high-value tire market, yet Pirelli’s market share there lags behind Europe and Asia.
  * **Current Footprint:** Only 5% of Pirelli’s U.S. sales are manufactured domestically; 55% come from Mexico, and 40% are imported from Europe and South America.
  * **Resilience Over Tariffs:** Pirelli is investing $1 billion to expand its plant in Rome, Georgia, scaling production from under 500,000 tires today to 6 million tires in seven years to insulate against tariffs, currency volatility, and logistics costs.

## Leadership, Culture & Personal Philosophy
* **From Apprentice to CEO:** Casaluci joined Pirelli as an apprentice in 2002 and was appointed CEO in 2023 after 21 years, succeeding Marco Tronchetti Provera. He emphasizes knowing the vast majority of Pirelli’s 30,000 employees.
* **Collaborative Leadership:** Casaluci’s management style is built on trust, listening, and allowing teams to make—and learn from—mistakes (though not the same mistake twice).
* **Personal Balance & Routine:** He cites working too much when younger as his biggest personal mistake, advising others to stay present for family. He wakes at 7:00 AM, exercises for 50–60 minutes while listening to classical jazz (Chet Baker, Miles Davis) or classical music, and is an avid sailor who has crossed the Atlantic.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **MotoGP Sole Supplier:** Pirelli will become the sole tire supplier for MotoGP starting next year (*Andrea Casaluci*).
* **US Manufacturing Scale-Up:** Pirelli’s plant in Rome, Georgia, will scale up from under 500,000 tires to 6 million tires within 7 years (*Andrea Casaluci*).
* **Autonomous Driving Data:** Future autonomous driving decisions (braking vs. steering) will be 100% data-driven in real time, relying on grip-estimation software powered by smart tires like the Cyber Tire (*Andrea Casaluci*).

## Notable Quotes
> "Tires are the only point that touch the ground in a vehicle. And so all the vehicle performance go through tires." — **Andrea Casaluci**

> "Some European suppliers came back after two months with the NDA to be signed... The Chinese came back with a physical prototype." — **Andrea Casaluci**

> "Europe just declared the target without helping with an industrial policy... In Norway, 90% or more of the new car registrations are electric vehicles. Why? You have a fantastic industrial policy." — **Andrea Casaluci**

> "The most important ingredient we put in a tire... is the passion. The passion of people that manufacture and develop a product that will be a few weeks after in the most visible track race of the world." — **Andrea Casaluci**

items.title: Sam Altman on Jensen Huang, Anthropic’s IPO, And Growing AI Backlash | Future Proof
items.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman addressed the fallout from Jensen Huang’s ouster at Nvidia, confirmed OpenAI will eventually go public despite the downsides, and warned that "double counting" in the chip supply chain and a severe memory shortage are creating complex bottlenecks.
items.content_text:
## TL;DR
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman addressed the fallout from Jensen Huang’s ouster at Nvidia, confirmed OpenAI will eventually go public despite the downsides, and warned that "double counting" in the chip supply chain and a severe memory shortage are creating complex bottlenecks. He also attributed growing voter backlash against AI data centers to the industry's failure to assure the public that humans—not AI—will remain in control of the future.

---

## Jensen Huang, Nvidia, and Market Stability
* **Reaction to Huang’s Ouster:** Altman declined to say whether Huang should return to Nvidia, noting he doesn't know enough to answer, but called Huang a longtime hero ("Heroes have flaws") and expressed strong personal empathy given his own board ouster roughly three years ago.
* **Nvidia’s $105B Guarantee:** When host Reed Albergotti asked if Nvidia’s $105 billion guarantee for OpenAI’s Ohio data center is still solid, Altman called Nvidia a "behemoth" whose guarantees people still trust, though he acknowledged Nvidia and Huang are deeply associated.
* **Industry Resilience:** Despite the leadership upheaval, Altman argued that end-user demand and revenue growth are now strong enough that the broader AI industry will be fine.

## Public Markets & Anthropic’s IPO
* **OpenAI’s IPO Plans:** Altman confirmed OpenAI will go public at some point. While there are real downsides to being public during a volatile, high-stakes period for AI safety, he believes it is directionally good for the broader world—not just private-market investors—to have exposure.
* **Investor Demand:** Pushing back on Albergotti’s suggestion of investor skepticism around Anthropic’s upcoming IPO, Altman said skepticism comes mostly from journalists while investors remain bullish. He dismissed concerns about OpenAI going public after Anthropic, noting that over the past year there has been "way too much investor demand and not enough supply."

## Supply Chain Bottlenecks & Memory Shortages
* **"Double Counting" in Chips:** Clarifying his closed-door remarks to Samsung executives, Altman explained that historically there was one main chip provider, making demand forecasting simple. Now, multiple chipmakers are talking to the silicon supply chain assuming OpenAI, Anthropic, and others will buy *all* of their chips.
* **Shifting Constraints:** At massive scale, OpenAI’s bottlenecks have shifted unpredictably between memory, rack assembly, data center capacity, and random components like PCB laminate.
* **Consumer RAM & $7T Capex:** Addressing backlash over his comments on home computer RAM, Altman said he wants people to have plenty of RAM for home tinkering. However, he noted OpenAI warned years ago about a coming memory squeeze and the need for $7 trillion in capex. Because the industry underbuilt, DRAM prices have jumped roughly 5X to 7X.
  * **Historical reluctance:** Memory vendors have been hesitant to commit capex because the business has historically been "invest $20 billion and make $19 billion" through booms and busts, though Altman expects production to ramp up significantly now.
  * **Cloud vs. Edge:** In a supply shortage, Altman argued it is more optimal to share memory in the cloud at 100% utilization rather than having it sit idle in edge devices.

## AI Backlash, Data Centers, and Politics
* **Why Voters Hate Data Centers:** Following a Democratic "blue wave" in which all but one data center referendum bill passed, Altman blamed the backlash on a terrible industry "sales pitch"—promising cures for cancer and cheap goods in exchange for humans losing agency and "liv[ing] like a Labrador."
  * **Staying "Team Human":** Altman urged the AI industry to take a firm stance against any gradual or sudden "handover" of control to AI, ensuring humans remain in control of the future.
* **Data Center Build-Out & Debt:** Altman maintained that data centers will still get built (potentially further from communities, such as in the desert), and the ecosystem will adapt to local concerns. He dismissed fears that debt-funded build-outs are a "house of cards," pointing to unprecedented actual revenue growth and margins, while acknowledging there will be some "foam on the top."
* **Political Stance:** Altman reaffirmed his July 2025 comment that he is "politically homeless" and that Democrats have lost the culture of innovation, though he intends to work with whoever is elected. He noted he last spoke with Donald Trump at the China state dinner.

## Security, Safety, and Product Lock-In
* **Espionage & "Pragmatic Centrists":** Addressing past security incidents (including hidden cameras/microphones in conference rooms and foreign agents trying to extract pre-training secrets over drinks), Altman said OpenAI takes a "pragmatic centrist" approach to safety—neither building in total secret nor pretending AI is like any other technology.
* **Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI):** OpenAI is using its technology to build new models faster, but is *not* pushing a button for unmonitored rapid self-improvement. Altman said holding back on RSI is a deliberate tactic to keep humans in control.
* **External Evaluators:** OpenAI is working with embedded evaluators, including METR. Altman could not confirm METR's report that Anthropic doubled its capability development speed, noting progress is still too "jagged" across tasks to generalize.
* **Dots & Data Lock-In:** Responding to Albergotti’s concern that OpenAI's *Dots* product stores user memory in the cloud without export or edit controls, Altman agreed in principle that users should own and be able to export their data (as they can with ChatGPT memory). However, he noted that *Dots*' nuanced understanding of a user's life is harder to export than an iPhone camera roll (100,000 photos) or iMessage.

## The Next Wave: AI for Science
* **Beyond Chatbots and Coding:** OpenAI recently expanded free compute for academic researchers. Altman highlighted the progression from chatbots to coding agents to "AI for science"—solving historically difficult math theorems and accelerating physics, chemistry, material science, and chip design.
* **Compressing Progress:** Altman’s goal is to use AI and compute to compress 10 or 100 years of scientific discovery into a single year.

---

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* "We will go public at some point." — Sam Altman (on OpenAI)
* "I think we will see production get ramped up a lot." — Sam Altman (on memory/chip production)
* "I think data centers will get built." — Sam Altman (on overcoming local opposition)
* "I think that the next couple of generations of models are really going to surprise people on the upside of how much they can be an engine of scientific discovery." — Sam Altman

---

## Notable Quotes
> "Jensen has long been a hero of mine. Heroes have flaws... It's hard to imagine the AI revolution without Jensen." — Sam Altman

> "If the sales pitch is like, we are going to offer you a cure to cancer and cheap stuff and the price of that is you are going to lose all agency and control and voice in the future, you are going to live like a Labrador... I think it's a terrible sales pitch. I don't want that world." — Sam Altman

> "I have never seen the actual revenue growth, including great margins, show up for any revolution in tech that I have witnessed in my career." — Sam Altman (on why AI data center debt is not a house of cards)

items.title: Satya Nadella opens Microsoft Ignite 2026
